bounded_leaf_result.tested_scope: Abstract targets only. In-scope targets provide: (A) atomic uniqueness or conditional commit keyed by witness w, (B) durable binding from w to payload digest d, (C) durable target-side evidence readable after the write path that exposes w and d or equivalent committed object contents, and (D) a target-authoritative read path for that committed evidence. No claim is made for targets lacking retained idempotency keys, atomic uniqueness, durable witness-to-payload binding, or readable commit evidence.

state_machine.transition: commit(w,d) may atomically transition ABSENT(w) to COMMITTED(w,d,r) once. Same-witness same-digest retries cannot create a second committed effect. Same-witness different-digest retries cannot overwrite the binding and are conflicts.
state_machine.ack_success: An acknowledged write is admitted as successful only after target evidence E(w) is read and binds the same witness to digest d or equivalent committed contents.
state_machine.ack_loss: After acknowledgement loss, retry safety and commit proof separate. Witness uniqueness suppresses duplicate effects, but it does not prove the first commit succeeded. Commit success is proven only when E(w) independently shows durable target evidence bound to w,d. Absent or unverifiable E(w) remains unresolved.
state_machine.concurrent_retry: Concurrent same-witness same-digest attempts converge to at most one committed effect under atomic uniqueness. Each contender must accept success only from target evidence matching w,d; duplicate rejection or a local success response without readable target evidence is insufficient after acknowledgement loss.
state_machine.payload_mismatch: Evidence E(w) with d_other != d is a conflict, never success or a safe duplicate of the intended payload.

bounded_leaf_result.result: Within the tested abstract scope, witness-keyed target-side idempotency plus durable readable target evidence is sufficient to distinguish at-most-once duplicate suppression from proof of successful target commit after acknowledgement loss. Witness-keyed idempotency without durable readable target evidence is sufficient only for duplicate suppression, not commit proof.
unresolved_conditions: Targets without atomic witness uniqueness remain unresolved for at-most-once effect safety.
Targets that retain idempotency state but expose no durable readable w-to-d evidence remain unresolved for proof of successful commit after acknowledgement loss.
Targets whose read path cannot establish target-authoritative committed evidence remain unresolved; local acknowledgements or retry rejection cannot substitute for commit proof.
